claims.text: It is the tentative name of a glass-*core materials* joint venture between Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Sumitomo Chemical's Korean subsidiary Dongwoo Fine-Chem, announced 2 July 2026
the acronym encodes Glass + Samsung + Sumitomo + Electronic + Materials

a company tentatively named GlaSSEM, capitalised at 482,100 million won, owned 66% by Samsung Electro-Mechanics and 34% by Dongwoo Fine-Chem, sited in Pyeongtaek ... with a supply system to be established by the second half of fiscal 2027

SEMCO said it on its own Q2 2026 earnings call, in the phrase 본격 가동 — full-scale operation — and it is the first specific mass-production year the company has ever given through an investor-relations channel
SEMCO's own published Q2 2026 earnings deck and newsroom release contain no reference to glass substrates, the joint venture, or 2028 at all
SCHOTT sells a single 510 × 515 mm format in four CTE grades from 3.2 to 7.2 ppm/K, with total thickness variation guaranteed only to 10–20 µm and warp to 100–200 µm
Nippon Electric Glass's glass-ceramic cores run 6.1–8.9 ppm/°C and it chose 515 × 510 mm explicitly so customers could reuse installed display-heritage equipment and "reduce capital investment"
It holds up to $75 million in CHIPS direct funding against $343 million of expected capex for a 120,000 sq ft Covington, Georgia facility, plus a separate $100 million NAPMP award
The US government's project page still says "first deliveries to customers are expected in 2025 and production capacity is expected to kick in 2027."
SKC has been loss-making for fifteen consecutive quarters and earmarked over ₩600 billion of rights-offering proceeds for customer evaluation, yield improvement and equipment.

as of SKC's Q2 2026 call on 27 July, Absolics samples had progressed substrate-level testing in Georgia and electrical evaluation in Japan, and had only just begun *initial* package-level reliability evaluation in Taiwan
LG Innotek's CEO said the quiet part: development is "completed," but "current demand is still insufficient to absorb the full production capacity such an investment would create."

Ibiden's February 2026 board notice commits approximately ¥500 billion across fiscal 2026–2028 to high-performance IC package substrates ... with a ¥220 billion first phase at the Gama plant and mass production from fiscal 2027. The release does not contain the word glass.
AT&S disclosed that a €1.5–2.0 billion expansion is "fully covered by long-term customer commitments," raised its revenue growth guidance from 30–35% to 45–55%, and tripled its capex plan.
with a 4.8 ppm/°C glass core, accumulated inelastic strain in the corner solder joint reached **19% per cycle**, against **8.43%** for an organic core
{label: "Glass core raised toward 10 ppm/°C", value: "~8%/cycle", pct: 42}
the strain study is simulation on a 20 × 20 mm substrate, published by authors associated with the organic-substrate incumbency, with no cycles-to-failure measured
Measured adhesion of copper to bare glass is 72 ± 18 gf/cm against an industry threshold above 500; an engineered porous titania promoter reaches 1,392 ± 64 gf/cm, but at a 600 °C sinter
A peer-reviewed process needed roughly **nine hours in 8 mol/L KOH at 110 °C** to open vias in 100 µm glass even at 333× selectivity
At ECTC 2026 STATS ChipPAC reported that 74 × 74 mm glass-core packages **failed every reliability test segment without edge coating**, and that edge coating cut warpage 33.5%.
its 510 × 515 mm, 24-layer glass-core panel with copper-filled TGVs, embedded EMIB bridges and optical waveguides was **processed on existing organic-substrate lines**

TSMC's CoWoS ladder runs from 1.5 reticles in 2016 to 3.3, then 5.5 on a 100 × 100 mm substrate with 12 HBM4 stacks, to roughly 9.5 reticles in 2027 on a body beyond 120 × 120 mm, to 14 reticles in 2028. Every step in that published roadmap specifies an organic substrate.

asked what constrains AI packaging, a TSMC packaging executive named memory shortages and tight ABF substrate supply over the next few years ... The 5.5-reticle generation is reported in mass production above 98% yield.
ASE targets AI-facing 310 × 310 mm FOCoS production around end-2026.
As of August 2026, no chip designer or substrate supplier has publicly disclosed a signed supply agreement, capacity reservation, or qualified design-in for a glass-core substrate. Not one.
Its largest "glass" commitment is the May 2026 Corning partnership — which covers optical fiber, connectivity and photonics, and never uses the words substrate or packaging.

The only named AMD employee on record, senior fellow Deepak Kulkarni, calls glass a technology with "enormous potential for the future of energy-efficient AI compute" — the language of an evaluation, not a design-in.
Both trace to a single Korean exclusive sourced to an unnamed industry official, partially corroborated by a paywalled DigiTimes line.
a 120 × 120 mm package fits 16 to a 510 × 515 mm panel at ~88% utilisation versus 2 per 300 mm wafer at ~41%
On new 2026–2028 capacity commitments, the organic column runs to roughly $5.7–6.3 billion against roughly $0.4 billion of fresh glass money: about 14×.
Yole's glass-core estimate for 2030 — a few hundred million dollars inside a $31 billion advanced-IC-substrate market — implies roughly 1.5% penetration at the end of the decade.
Glass-substrate 2030 estimates span more than an order of magnitude, from Yole's "multi-hundred-million" for glass core specifically to Counterpoint's $8.1 billion
In 2019 Samsung Electro-Mechanics sold its panel-level packaging business — built for ₩264 billion ... to Samsung Electronics for ₩785 billion
Korea named next-generation glass package substrates as a cooperation model only on 6 August 2026 ... inside a ₩91 billion five-year envelope shared across five projects
TSMC's first published glass validation on an 85 × 110 mm five-reticle package showed 16% better warpage alongside 27% lower power-supply resistance and 42% lower inductance.
SEMCO's disclosed coupon: 40 µm TGVs, 8 build-up layers on a 640 µm core, 80 × 80 mm body. Board- and system-level reliability "as yet unknown."
Nvidia's response to exactly this problem on Rubin Ultra was reportedly to *reduce* die count rather than adopt glass
It is roughly 4% of SEMCO's FY2025 revenue and about 6% of the ₩8 trillion multi-year Sejong pledge.
